solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Misconceive women's pause while speaking

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a rest is a pause, here a break taken mid-speech

explanation.surface: Someone misunderstands a woman who hesitates as she talks.
explanation.walkthrough: The W of WREST is silent, so the answer itself is spoken just like the pause it contains.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest words is to twist their meaning, which amounts to misconstruing or distorting them deliberately.

clue.text: Unconventional show with Henry on a collection of lives?

indicators.note: something unconventional departs from the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for with
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
o' is a contracted form of on, as in o'nights

explanation.surface: An offbeat programme with a man called Henry is built around a set of biographies.
explanation.walkthrough: Lives here means biographies, which is the joke behind the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Who's Who is the annual reference book of short biographies of notable people, literally a gathered set of life stories.

clue.text: They give oversight on struggle with chap that is small

parts.note: re means on or concerning
to vie is to compete or struggle
W is the abbreviation for with
a bod is a person, a chap
i.e. stands for id est, that is
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Supervisors oversee a short man's fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Six short pieces in a row; the trap is reading 'on struggle' as a phrase rather than two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Review bodies are committees appointed to examine and supervise policies, pay or conduct, so their role is supervision.

clue.text: A core duty could be presented as didactic

indicators.note: these letters could be laid out in another form, so they get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A central obligation might come across as preachy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface feels like moral comment on duty; all nine letters of the first three words are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to instruct, which is exactly what an educatory text or approach sets out to do.

clue.text: Eruptions in chains? Time for frequency

indicators.note: one thing standing for another signals a swap of one letter in place of a second

parts.note: fetters are chains or shackles
T is the abbreviation for time
F is the symbol for frequency, the letter to be replaced

explanation.surface: Someone in shackles breaks out in rashes, with a remark about time and frequency.
explanation.walkthrough: Start from a word for chains and put T where its F was.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetter is an old name for a skin disease such as eczema or ringworm, a patch where the skin erupts.

clue.text: Old playwright recreated recent eccentricity

indicators.note: to recreate is to make afresh, so these letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic

explanation.surface: A classical dramatist revived a modern oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccentricity looks like part of the anagram's colour but is the mathematical symbol e, as used for ellipses.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman comic dramatist of the second century BC, so he is an ancient writer of plays.

clue.text: First to twist concerns over bit of shoe

indicators.note: first means the opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of to

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upward, so the word is read backward

parts.note: a part is a concern or interest, as in for my part

explanation.surface: The first thing to go wrong when a shoe twists is a worry about one of its pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: First applies to 'to', not 'twist'; 'twist' is just filler that also yields T.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-strap is the T-shaped strap across the instep of some shoes and sandals, so it is a component of footwear.

clue.text: Scots joke about one canine affected by a disease?

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word faces the other way

parts.note: bar (also baur) is a Scots word for a jest
Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for canine tooth in dental notation

explanation.surface: A Scotsman jokes about a dog that may have caught something.
explanation.walkthrough: Canine wants to be the dog in the disease story, but it just gives C; the dog is still apt as rabies spreads through bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabic means relating to or affected by rabies, the viral disease, and the question mark admits this is one specific illness.

clue.text: One such as Blofeld being nameless at first

indicators.note: lacking a label means the letter that abbreviates it goes missing from the word

parts.note: the Bond villain is Ernst Stavro Blofeld
N is the abbreviation for name, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A Bond villain is anonymous at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Blofeld's first name is Ernst; remove the N to get the old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic adverb meaning formerly or originally, the sense of at the beginning or earlier.

clue.text: Pass a motion in secret and peer endlessly into issue?

indicators.note: without ends means both outer letters are dropped

parts.note: cover is concealment, as in under cover

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: an issue of the Financial Times, the FT
the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A vote is passed behind closed doors as a nobleman pokes into a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is parliamentary, but pass a motion means relieve oneself: to cover the feet is the biblical euphemism for doing so (Judges 3:24). The FT is the Financial Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: In the King James Bible, covering one's feet is a polite euphemism for defecating, the bodily sense of passing a motion.

clue.text: Wartime inflatable parent childishly dumped near to Scots

indicators.note: something dumped is thrown away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a Mae West was an inflatable life jacket used by Second World War airmen
ma is a child's word for mother, the letters thrown out

explanation.surface: A wartime balloon is abandoned by a childish parent close to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The life jacket was nicknamed after the busty film star Mae West; drop the MA at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewest is a Scots dialect word meaning close by or nearby, so it renders near in that language.

clue.text: Flier in distress keeping special advantage first

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: to harrow is to distress or torment
an edge is an advantage
SP is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A pilot in trouble keeps a special advantage in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' puts the advantage before the special, and both go inside the word for distress after its H.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedge sparrow, or dunnock, is a small brown European bird, and a flier is crossword shorthand for any bird.

clue.text: Never run away from deal after backing strong posts

indicators.note: to back is to go in reverse, so the order is turned around

parts.note: bitts are strong posts on a ship's deck for fastening cables

indicators.note: taking something away from a word means removing it

parts.note: to deal can mean to divide or part, as does sever
R is the cricket abbreviation for run, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Never flee from a bargain once you have backed a sturdy set of posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never' looks like part of an instruction but is the definition. The piece cut from the deal word comes after the reversed posts.
explanation.definitionFit: St Tib's Eve is a dialect expression for a day that will never come, as there is no such saint's day.

clue.text: Old language's inclusive term for tatpurusha

parts.note: inc. is the abbreviation for inclusive

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the Sanskrit grammatical term

explanation.surface: An ancient language has an all-embracing word for a Sanskrit type of compound.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatpurusha, a Sanskrit compound, is there only to supply its end letter; 'term' means end, not word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inca can name the Quechua language spoken by the Inca people of the old Andean empire.

clue.text: Strangeness in case of emergency driver

parts.note: S is the physics symbol for the quantum number strangeness
ICE stands for In Case of Emergency, the phone contact

explanation.surface: Something odd about the person you would call to drive in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Strangeness is a particle-physics quantity written S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sice, or syce, is an Indian groom who tends horses and drives a carriage, so a sort of coachman.

clue.text: One avowed of obedience casts arm of Japanese

parts.note: a nun takes vows including obedience
to chuck is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: A vowed religious throws off a Japanese person's limb.
explanation.walkthrough: Arm is a weapon, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nunchucks are a martial-arts weapon of two sticks joined by a chain, associated with Okinawa and Japan.

clue.text: Move to and fro in White Horse, say, sheltering last of these

indicators.note: to shelter something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: white horses are foam-capped waves at sea

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of these

explanation.surface: A rider sways about inside a pub called the White Horse, protecting the last of them.
explanation.walkthrough: White Horse reads like a pub or the chalk figure, but white horses are crested waves.
explanation.definitionFit: To weave is to dodge from side to side, as a boxer or a driver through traffic sways back and forth.

clue.text: Entertain exploit involving bottle (maturity not needed)

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: an act is a deed or exploit

indicators.note: what is not needed is left out, so those letters go

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
age is maturity, the letters dropped

explanation.surface: Throwing a party is a feat that involves wine, and you needn't be grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is not the wine but British slang for courage; take AGE off it and put what remains inside the deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Accourt is a Spenserian word meaning to receive courteously or entertain a guest, from its link with court.

clue.text: Sea-bred officer behind veering west

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means travelling right to left, the opposite way

parts.note: prat is slang for the buttocks

explanation.surface: A naval officer raised at sea trails behind as his ship turns west.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind reads as a position but is the noun for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarp, short for tarpaulin, was once a naval officer who had risen from common sailor rather than gentleman stock.

clue.text: Crowded spikes are meant to be free

indicators.note: set free, the letters are loose to fall into a new order

parts.note: A is the symbol for the are, a metric unit of area
taken as written

explanation.surface: Packed rows of spikes are supposed to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: Are looks like a verb but is the metric unit of 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenta are catkins, dense hanging flower clusters, which botanists describe as spikes packed with tiny flowers.

clue.text: Mumper to mutter, "Up in the morning and out"

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backward

parts.note: a.m. means in the morning
out cold is under, as under anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A beggar grumbles about rising early and heading outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Mumper is an old word for a beggar. Out means unconscious here, not outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Maunder was an old noun for a beggar and is a verb meaning to grumble or talk aimlessly, covering both sides.

clue.text: Anonymous old Italian magistrate, one involving deduction

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for anonymous
the priors were chief magistrates of medieval Florence
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An unnamed Italian official of old reasons things out.
explanation.walkthrough: A prior here is not a monk but a medieval Florentine magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from general principles to consequences, the classic pattern of deductive argument.

clue.text: One of the orchestra is filling old bottle

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: bot is an obsolete word for a leather bottle, like Spanish bota
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician pours into an antique flask.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes inside the word for bottle, after the O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, a double-reed woodwind instrument found in every symphony orchestra.

clue.text: Jolly small flock of sheep

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a jaunt or outing, a jolly in British slang
second meaning: a dialect word for a small flock of sheep or goats

explanation.walkthrough: Jolly looks like an adjective for the sheep, but it is the British noun for a pleasure outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is an excursion, which is what a jolly is in Britain, and in dialect it also names a little group of sheep.

clue.text: So, American boarded vessel plying the Levant

indicators.note: to board a ship is to get inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for so, thus
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: So, a Yank climbed aboard a ship trading in the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: So is the Latin sic, the editor's note meaning thus.
explanation.definitionFit: A saic is a type of ketch formerly common in the Levant, the eastern Mediterranean coastal region.

clue.text: Cuts being mostly cruel and ultimately pointless

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: severe means harsh or cruel, here missing its last letter

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of pointless

explanation.surface: Budget cuts are mostly cruel and in the end achieve nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuts reads as a noun for spending reductions, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut through or cut off, so the third-person form matches the verb cuts.

clue.text: Harrow, eg, returned rubbish Rector misplaced in Square

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters run backward

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: a misplaced letter has been put in the wrong spot, so the order changes

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rector
square means true, exact; the letters around the moving one

explanation.surface: At a school like Harrow, a returning pupil talks rubbish when the rector turns up in the quad.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow looks like the public school but is the verb meaning to distress. TRUE with its R moved gives the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow is to torment or distress someone, so it is one instance of what torture does.

clue.text: Genus of marsh plants going through fusty phases

indicators.note: something going through a phrase passes across its words, so the letters run inside them

parts.note: inside the two words, across the gap

explanation.surface: Swamp plants pass through musty stages.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of fusty into the start of phases.
explanation.definitionFit: Typha is the botanical genus of bulrushes or reedmace, tall plants that grow in wetlands.

clue.text: Togs perhaps got from upper-class nanas

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage
a nana is British slang for a fool, as is a nit

explanation.surface: Posh grandmothers hand down clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Togs looks like clothes and nanas like grandmothers; a tog is a measure of the warmth of a duvet, and a nana is a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tog is a unit for measuring thermal insulation, so togs are examples of measurement units.

clue.text: Surging oil well without good marshal

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a gusher is an oil well that spouts freely
G is the abbreviation for good, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A spouting oil well, with nothing good about it, is controlled by a marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal is the verb here, as a steward guides people to seats.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher people is to guide or escort them into position, the same as marshalling a crowd.

clue.text: Anger about politician's term is concerning

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: a term is an end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of politician

explanation.surface: Fury over a politician's period in office is a matter of concern.
explanation.walkthrough: Term looks like a stint in office but means end, as in the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In re is legal Latin meaning in the matter of, used in the same way as about or regarding.

clue.text: Mystic — one to make a song and dance about being cut

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter goes
about can mean turned round, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: a fuss is a song and dance; shortened
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A holy man is someone who will complain loudly about being slashed.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a song and dance is British idiom for making a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi follows the mystical, contemplative tradition within Islam, so is a religious mystic.

clue.text: Morse or the like is one who rambles about apron? Vice versa

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another
the opposite arrangement holds, so outer and inner roles swap

parts.note: a pinnie or pinny is a pinafore, an apron
ped is short for pedestrian, a walker

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse, or someone like him, wanders around in an apron.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is not the detective or the code but an old name for the walrus. Vice versa puts the apron around the walker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnipede, or pinniped, is a fin-footed sea mammal such as a seal or walrus.

clue.text: Judge it next to one smashing flirt

parts.note: a judge hears a case
't is an old contraction of it, as in 'tis
one who smashes is a breaker

explanation.surface: Rate this beside a stunning person who toys with lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 't for it is the old contraction found in 'tis and 'twas.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartbreaker charms people and then lets them down, much as a flirt toys with admirers' affections.

clue.text: Self-discipline caused by second one being in lost cases

indicators.note: being inside means placed within the other piece
something lost is astray, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: Roman numeral one
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Restraint is the result of a runner-up being involved in cases that were lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Lost reads as cases that failed in court, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascesis is the practice of rigorous self-denial and training, the ascetic's method of mastering oneself.

clue.text: Fried dish, it's gold when flipped

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the letters run backward

parts.note: it's without the apostrophe
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A fried dish turns golden when you toss it in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping is exactly what a cook does to this dish, which hides the instruction in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss potato cake of grated potato fried in a pan until crisp.
